concerns: Manufacturability/yield risk: conservative TMP/flux limits and added depth filtration may materially reduce recovery; pilot runs on manufacturing‑representative cassettes are required to confirm acceptable qualitative/quantitative yields before GMP adoption.

Process sensitivity and scale‑up risk: cassette rotation, depth filter performance, and per‑cassette TMP limits must be transferably implementable and reproducible on production hardware; consumable variability (filter lots, membrane chemistry) could reintroduce variability.

Measurement feasibility and assay interference: immuno‑capture and protection assays are feasible but depend critically on validated capture‑compatibility with process buffers and robust spike‑in tracer recovery; without these controls, assay artifacts (capture incompatibility or tracer loss) could be mistaken for true membrane damage.

Lot comparability and statistical power: proposal requires >=3 independent conditioned‑medium lots matched for source‑cell passage and upstream parameters; without this, attribution of signature preservation/loss to TFF envelope versus upstream variability is ambiguous.

Stability and downstream QA relevance: preservation of an intact‑EV analytical signature is necessary but not sufficient for downstream potency or in‑vivo exposure—Driedonks et al. indicate preserved material may still fail to reach or be detected in target tissues in larger species; bridging studies (in‑vivo recoverability/pk) will be needed to connect manufacturing gate to clinical relevance.

Analytical workflow complexity and throughput: the orthogonal workflow (fractionation + particle counts + capture + protection assays) is moderate complexity and may limit throughput for routine in‑process control; feasibility as a routine manufacturing gate depends on assay streamlining/qualification.
conclusion: Supported as a plausible, implementable mitigation for a processing-sensitive intact‑EV identity loss risk, provided targeted analytical validation and pilot-scale yield studies are executed before adoption as a manufacturing gate. MISEV2023 supports the need for orthogonal intact‑EV analytics and process-sensitivity caution; the nonhuman-primate biodistribution data caution that preserved analytic signatures do not guarantee in‑vivo detectability and so do not substitute for downstream bridging. Key gaps: validated capture-compatibility controls/spike-in performance, quantitative pilot yields on representative GMP cassettes, and demonstration of lot-to-lot reproducibility (>=3 lots) under the proposed envelope.
evidence_gap: No direct experimental evidence provided that the proposed staged low‑shear TFF envelope preserves orthogonal intact‑EV signatures across >=3 independent conditioned‑medium lots at scale‑proxy volumes on manufacturing-representative cassettes; capture‑compatibility/spike‑in controls are not yet validated; pilot quantitative recovery/yield and stability data post‑concentration are missing.
